page.layout: One block of running text in a single column; in the left margin two marginal notes ("Eleemosyna" and "Spenda", the second beside the fourth paragraph's lower lines). Running head at top centre. No page number, catchword or signature printed on the scan.

main_text.p: suis fame dominante, tolerabili pretio frumē tum vendit, vt farciat eorum inopiam, & vt exteri quoque in publico foro fruges viliori pretio habere possint. Argetoratū vrbs ornatissima, hodie quoq; à multis celebratur, quòd in illa annonæ caritate, quæ fuit anno Dom. 1517. item 1529. aliisq; teporibus, suis ciuibus, & etiam peregrinis fruges liberaliter distribuit: suisq; ciuibus, aliisq; quos fames adipsos compulerat, quotidie alimoniā suppeditauit.

EleemosynaAdhæc magistratus officium est, curare vt publicæ eleemosynæ rectè distribuātur. In pagis Ecclesiæ aliquot, suos quoq; habent annuos reditus: utile igitur fuerit à procuratoribus illorum, ratione accepti & expensi exigere, ne dum diuites opibus illis vtuntur, aut ex illis belluantur, pauperes cibo, victuq; fraudētur. Multis in locis statis dieb. panes distribuuntur pauperibus, quam eleemosynā vulgo Spenda,Spendam vocant. Deriuatur, vel à Germanica voce, quæ expendere significat, vel à Græco vocabulo σπένδω, quod est, libo, vel sacrifico, & σπονδὴ libamen.
Neq; parum retulerit, vt magistratus pauperes

page.notes: Marginal note "Spenda," is printed in the left margin, beside "Spendam vocant" line; the Greek words are reproduced with the printed letters as far as legible (σπένδω and σπονδὴ are approximate readings of the scan, marked as doubtful). Final line "pauperes" is set flush right and is a line fragment carried to the next page. The Greek on "quod est" line is partly obscured; accents are uncertain. Several words in the first lines show faint ink; "Argetoratū" is printed so (Argentoratum). Words at the end of the first paragraph "alimoniā" and "suppeditauit" read as printed.
